project.name: oil-gas-compliance-agent
project.description: An agent for reviewing oil and gas pipeline network instrumentation and automatic-control specifications. It converts technical standards into retrievable, citable, executable knowledge via OCR, BM25, and embedding search, enabling evidence-backed Q&A and deterministic compliance pre-review. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces the oil-gas-compliance-agent: a RAG application that turns Chinese pipeline instrumentation and automatic-control specifications into a searchable, citable, executable knowledge base. It lays out the two core flows the rest of this tour follows — a question-answering path that retrieves evidence before answering, and a compliance pre-review path that decomposes design descriptions into atomic check items and executes deterministic rules. The module map (M0–M11) and directory structure here are the scaffolding for every step ahead.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: app/main.py is the FastAPI application factory that wires the three API routers (agent, qa, review), request-ID tracing middleware, and global AppError handling into a single ASGI app. Reading it gives the bird's-eye view of runtime structure: every HTTP surface for the Q&A and compliance flows is registered here before the server starts. It is the front door behind the README's architecture diagram.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's application-factory pattern builds and configures the app inside a function so tests can instantiate a fresh app with overridden dependencies; the request-ID middleware sets a contextvar that propagates through every logged request for traceability.

tour.title: Shared Domain Vocabulary
tour.description: app/domain/models.py is the most depended-upon file in the codebase (51 inbound references) and defines the enums and Pydantic models shared across every layer: knowledge units, evidence, check items, rules, and compliance results. Because services, API routes, and repositories all import these types, this file is the contract that keeps the ingestion, retrieval, QA, and compliance subsystems speaking one language. Understanding it early makes every downstream module easier to read.
tour.languageLesson: Centralized Pydantic domain models act as a typed vocabulary: enums and field validators encode business rules once, so serialization, validation, and documentation stay consistent across the API and data layers.

tour.title: Core Infrastructure
tour.description: The core layer provides cross-cutting plumbing used everywhere: nested pydantic-settings configuration, OpenAI-compatible chat and embedding clients, a domain-specific exception taxonomy, and redacting JSON logging. These files define how the system talks to LLMs and how failures surface, so they underpin both the Q&A and compliance flows introduced in the README. The model client in particular is the only place raw LLM calls are made.
tour.languageLesson: pydantic-settings reads environment variables into a typed, nested settings tree, so each subsystem consumes validated config objects instead of raw strings or scattered os.environ lookups.

tour.title: Knowledge Ingestion Pipeline
tour.description: This is the PDF-to-structure front of the data flow. The pipeline renders PDF pages, runs CPU OCR (RapidOCR), writes traceable JSONL output, and caches completed pages, while the structure parser recovers the clause hierarchy, tables, terms, and figures and emits knowledge units. These structured units are exactly what the knowledge layer indexes next and what retrieval searches later.

tour.title: Knowledge Storage and Indexing
tour.description: Where structured knowledge becomes queryable. The SQLite repository stores knowledge units and supports exact clause and table lookup, while the builder assembles BM25 and vector indexes and the index module implements ranking with a deterministic hash embedding fallback. This is the STORE and VECTOR node of the README's architecture diagram — the substrate every later query and answer depends on.

tour.title: Retrieval Service
tour.description: The retrieval layer turns a user question into a RetrievalPlan: it analyzes and decomposes the query, routes explicit clause/table identifiers to exact lookup and open semantic questions to BM25 and vector candidates fused via RRF. The agentic planner adds decomposition into retrieval goals and identifier enforcement — the evidence-acquisition half of the project's evidence-first contract.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges BM25 and vector result lists by rank rather than raw score, sidestepping the incomparable score scales of lexical and semantic retrievers.

tour.title: Evidence-Grounded Q&A
tour.description: Here the project's core constraint becomes concrete: the chat model never touches the database directly — it calls the knowledge_search tool, which returns Evidence objects with clause IDs, page numbers, and source text. Building on Step 7's retrieval, the QA service validates citations and engineering values before composing an answer and safely declines when evidence is insufficient. This is the evidence-first 'cite before you answer' discipline from the README.

tour.title: Design Decomposition and Clarification
tour.description: This branch handles the compliance flow's input. The design parser splits natural-language design descriptions into structured check items (with an LLM-backed fallback), and the clarification service and session detect missing fields, drive follow-up questions, and re-check completeness within round limits. This is the DESIGN to ITEMS to CONFIRM segment of the README's second flow.

tour.title: Deterministic Compliance Engine
tour.description: Once check items exist from Step 9, this engine evaluates them with no model in the loop. Candidate rules are extracted from compliance evidence, then threshold, range, enum, boolean, lookup, and composite comparison strategies run against them with engineering unit conversion. The matcher scores rules against check items and flags missing conditions and conflicts to produce the pre-review report.

tour.title: Workflow Orchestration
tour.description: The LangGraph state machine ties the two flows into a single agent. nodes.py implements per-step logic — intent classification, retrieval, compliance review, and answer generation — while routes.py decides the next node from intent and evidence coverage, and graph.py builds and runs the machine. This is the runtime brain that coordinates everything from Steps 6 through 10.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph models an agent as a graph of nodes joined by conditional edges over a shared AgentState, so bounded retrieval retries and confirmation loops are expressed as graph cycles rather than imperative while-loops.

tour.title: API Layer and Web UI
tour.description: The routers registered in Step 2 come to life here. agent.py exposes the workflow session lifecycle, messaging, and report export; review.py exposes design preview, clarification, candidate-rule review, and rule evaluation endpoints; and index.html is the self-contained single-page chat UI. Together they are the user-facing surface of both the Q&A and compliance flows.

tour.title: Reproducible Evaluation
tour.description: The evaluation subsystem makes the whole pipeline verifiable. generated.py synthesizes retrieval, tool-call, design, rule, and end-to-end datasets from stored knowledge units, and runner.py executes the retrieval, QA, design, and compliance suites with version binding to the code hash. The report.md stop records the measured metrics across the seven M11 evaluation tracks, closing the loop on correctness.

tour.title: Containerization and Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the app with a multi-stage build: a builder stage pre-compiles Python dependencies into wheels, and the runtime stage installs them alongside the ONNX Runtime and OCR system libraries. docker-compose.yml builds and runs that image with CPU/memory limits and mounts the source tree. This is how the application described across this tour actually ships and runs.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate build-time dependencies (compiling wheels) from the runtime image so production ships only what the server needs; Compose then pins CPU/memory limits for the OCR and embedding workloads.
